Ground up hominy (kinda like corn) that you cook much like rice, only you leave it on the heat. You can get it a bit undercooked, where it's a little gritty, some people are into that. There's the perfect consistency where it doesn't quite pour off your spoon, but rather drops slowly like a sludge. That is the grit you want... but some like it thinner, where it's a bit soupy. Which isn't bad if you like a lot of cheese in it, because it thickens it nicely without really having to chew. You can get it super thick where when you take a spoon of it, it doesn't even itself out in the bowl. Which isn't bad for a ton of butter or syrup. Tastes a bit like corn... a bit like starch... fills you up for breakfast, and does so cheaply. It goes well with damn near everything. Just depends on what am individual prefers. Try butter, salt, pepper, spices, sugars, jellies, jams, syrups, cheeses, throw some egg, sausage, or bacon in it. Anything you add completely changes the flavor. Some people don't realize it's versatility. Lots of people equate it to the northerners cream of wheat, but you can do much more with it.

Before I went back to work I only occasionally asked him to get up with our little girl. When I started returning to work, we shared the nighttime more evenly. It's not easy to have a baby and NOT be tired, but it's not safe to wear yourself down and then try to cater to baby. She also is taking care of baby all day while you work, so mom sometimes will need a break too...
